project: (note) Headless full-boot TUI tests (AgentCli with useTui: true) MUST pass `tuiProgramHooks: TuiProgramHooks(input: keys.stream, output: frames, width:, height:)` in AgentCliConfig — without it the dart_tui program writes to FakeCliIO's stdout and the _FrameSink stays empty forever, so every frames.text waitFor spins to timeout. Working twins: agent_hub_overlay_guard_test.dart, agent_cli_tui_sync_test.dart. Also anchor any injected waitingClock at DateTime.now(), never a pinned past date (overdue-timer storm starves the REPL loop). [#note,#source_agent,testing,tui,integration-test,gotcha]
project: (note) curl's internal `--retry N` does NOT resume with `-C -`: on a timed-out attempt it starts over from offset 0, truncating the partial output (verified locally against a throttling range server — transfer restarted at 0 with `--retry 2 -C - --max-time 2`). To make a bounded, resumable download, own the retries in a bash loop and give curl only `-C - --max-time <budget>`; `rm -f` the partial file before the loop so `-C -` resumes only your own bytes. Budget arithmetic for GH Actions: attempts*max_time + (attempts-1)*sleep must fit the step's timeout-minutes (remember curl `--retry N` means N retries PLUS the initial attempt). [#note,#source_agent,ci,github-actions,curl,networking,workflows,gotcha]
project: (note) fa app-suite repair round (all under main checkout, ungated-clone-era debts): the flutter_app suite had 14 red tests+guards, ALL from other agents' hook-skipped commits — fixed in 0.1.239: (1) agent_service compaction-failure test expected 'transcript untouched' but the emergency _localTrimFallback (0.1.219, deliberate) honestly trims in-memory with a '[context trimmed locally…' marker while the session file keeps every record — test now asserts the marker + full records on disk; (2) session_chat_sheet drawer tests: FlutterSessionManager.openSession completes only over REAL async hops (widget-test fake clock doesn't advance it) — bounded drain loop `for(i<50 && activeId!=target) { await tester.runAsync(() => Future.delayed(10ms)); await pumpAndSettle(); }` after the tap; (3) map goldens: commit 4ea43d4e slimmed the bundle (map demo → fa_widgets catalog) — mapGolden + the controls-menu test now markTestSkipped when assets/apps/map/manifest.json is absent; (4) cli_visual ctrl+s test: shell-job ids are now sh-<n>-<uniq> — parse RegExp 'sh-[A-Za-z0-9-]+' from the /tasks screen and cancel the exact id (bare 'sh-1' → 'unknown job'); (5) cli_visual /agents inbox test: sessions live under <home>/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions (macOS default, bin/fah.dart _defaultSessionRoot prefers it when writable) — seed mail by searching both roots; (6) session_reuse: aa770722 made corrupt JSONL lines QUARANTINED (dropped + .corrupt sidecar), not fatal — test updated to 'loads with junk quarantined'; (7) WidgetsCatalogSheet failed golden_guard (no golden) + l10n_guard ('Install failed: $error', 'Retry'×2 hardcoded) — added widgetsCatalogInstallFailed/Offline/LoadFailed/Retry keys (en+ru), context.l10n routing (import l10n_ext.dart!), new test/golden/widgets_catalog_golden_test.dart (MockClient catalog, pumpGolden+expectGolden, 420x700 in goldenSizeTall) registered in golden_guard _coverage; gen-l10n regenerates app_localizations*.dart. Regenerated goldens MUST be eyeballed (apps_grid.png = 15 demo tiles, clean). Full app suite: 1356 passed / 44 skipped / 0 failed. [#note,#source_agent,fa,app-tests,golden,l10n,guards]
project: (note) fa 0.1.240 shipped (commit 0dc54496 on origin/main, installed): compaction-hang fix. Root cause of the ~58-min 'Compacting context…' spinner: a summarizer endpoint that accepts the request and never answers pends stream.result forever — provider connect/idle watchdogs (180s/5min) miss dribbling keep-alives and lost completions. Fix: AutoCompactor gained attemptBudget (default 10 min, ctor param) — every compactSession() attempt runs under Future.timeout; TimeoutException is non-transient (no retry spin), the pass falls to the next summarizer or the honest local trim, turn continues. Bonus fix found by the new test: the emergency local trim now zeroes kept AssistantMessage usage anchors (a stale generation-time anchor kept the post-trim estimate over the window and retriggered compaction every turn — same rule as the success pass). Two tests with a never-completing Completer summarizer drive both paths (rescue-via-trim, honest-failure-when-nothing-to-trim). Note: user's live hung session needs kill + `fa --session <id>` resume; new fa prevents recurrence. Push needed rebase (other agents pushed chore(release): v0.1.240 — landed cleanly). [#note,#source_agent,fa,compaction,hang,0.1.240]
project: (note) Google adapter now retries once on exact 400 'Unable to process input image' error by replacing inlineData images with text placeholder '(image omitted: the model backend could not decode it)' — allows agent to gracefully handle corrupt images [#note,#source_agent,400-error,image-placeholder,retry]
project: (note) Bundled demo apps were removed from the app bundle entirely; the catalog is now the only source of widgets and Reset apps returns an empty grid. [#note,#source_agent,demos,reset,catalog-only]
project: (note) CPU-шторм fa: корень — overflow в HubClient.defaultBackoff (`1 << (attempt-1)` даёт ноль с attempt 65+), вызывая вечный tight-loop реконнектов к несуществующему хабу ws://127.0.0.1:8787; фикс — clamp до сдвига, регрессионный тест test/backoff_overflow_test.dart. ```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

blocks.text:
Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

```dart

```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

```dart

There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

Wait — there's a problem with the cancellation semantics for the legacy behavior. The OLD code:

```dart
while (_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < config.maxEmptyRetries && !(cancelToken?.isCancelled ?? false))
```

Old: an empty + cancelled token → while doesn't run → return empty message → settle → exit 0 (silently). New: E5 conversion → aborted terminal. That's the intended E5 fix. But does any existing pinned test rely on cancel+empty returning the empty? Let me search later when running tests.

Also — the `StopReason.toolUse` case: a toolUse message with ONLY tool calls → `isEmptyAssistantCompletion` false (ToolCall) → notEmpty ✓. But hmm — WAIT. There's a subtle issue with `classifyEmptyCompletion` being called on EVERY turn in the while loop, including HEALTHY toolUse/text messages (the loop entry: current = the just-streamed message; verdict notEmpty → break immediately). That's an extra classification per turn — pure, cheap (window scan from the tail to the last user message). Fine.

But CAREFUL — a subtle bug: the `while (!cancelled)` loop entry runs classify on EVERY iteration INCLUDING the very first message which might be healthy — fine, breaks.

Another subtlety: the FIRST empty in a clean window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app default): generic=0 <1 → generic++ → stream → empty again → generic=1 == max → classify: cleanEmpty → break ✓ (old behavior: retries(1) == max(1) → break) ✓.

And for a hiccup window with maxEmptyRetries=1 (app): empty → generic++ → stream → empty → generic==max → verdict emptyAfterPartial → hiccup=0 <3 → backoff → stream... → up to 3 hiccup retries → exhaustion error with attempts = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. OK.

This test ("an auto-continued run that answers empty gets the continue nudge") is a REAL regression risk: the scripted sequence is toolTurn (tool activity!) → relief 'S' → funnel 'S' → EMPTY → expects the 'continue' nudge (call 5) answering 'nudged continuation fine'.

With my change, the empty turn after TOOL ACTIVITY classifies `emptyAfterPartial` → the LOOP (maxEmptyRetries=0) skips generic, then hiccup-retries: empty #2 would consume call 5 (which the test expects to be the NUDGE with prompt 'continue'), then empty #3, #4, exhaustion error — the test's `fake.calls == 5` and nudge assertions would break... AND MORE IMPORTANTLY — is the test's semantic still desired?? 

Per gh-1577: an empty after tool activity is EXACTLY the incident shape — it should hiccup-retry, NOT nudge. This pinned test pins the OLD (buggy) behavior... but wait — does it? The test's intent is #1085 M2b: "auto-continued runs get the nudge like any run". The scenario: over-window relief → auto-continued run → empty answer. The turn HAS tool activity (the tool turn at the start) — so under gh-1577 the empty is a hiccup (bounded retry), and the nudge would only fire for clean empties.

Hmm — this is a genuine semantic CONFLICT between the old pinned test and the new card. The ticket says: "AC2 — A clean empty completion with no partial content anywhere in the turn keeps today's behavior exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle." — this test's empty is NOT clean (tool activity in the turn). So the test needs UPDATING to reflect the new classification: either the scripted history changes so the empty is genuinely clean (hard — the whole point is the over-window funnel), or the test now expects the hiccup behavior (retries then... the 'continue' nudge never fires → the test's M2b assertion needs a clean-empty variant).

Wait — let me think about what the RIGHT behavior is for this scenario post-gh-1577: over-window funnel auto-continues the run; the continuation comes back EMPTY after a turn full of tool activity. gh-1577: hiccup → 3 in-loop retries (backoff) → if still empty → run error (loud). The nudge path is not involved. The M2b property ("auto-continued runs get the nudge like any run") survives for CLEAN empties — which the agent_cli_test.dart REG-1 tests already pin (they're plain textTurn('') with no tools).

So this pinned test needs a rework: the empty after the funnel continuation is now a hiccup. Options:
(a) Change the scripted continuation-empty to a CLEAN empty: impossible — the turn includes the tool turn (same logical turn; the funnel's continuation is an auto-continue within the same logical user turn).

Hmm wait — actually, what IS "the turn" for the classifier here? The window = messages after the last UserMessage. In this scenario: user 'go' → toolTurn → relief/funnel 'S' (assistant texts) → empty. All after the last UserMessage → window has tool activity + text → emptyAfterPartial. Yes — hiccup.

(b) Update the test to pin the NEW behavior: the empty continuation gets hiccup-retried; script [toolTurn, 'S', 'S', empty, healthy('nudged continuation fine' → 'continued fine')] — the loop recovers via retry (call 5 = in-loop retry, context has NO 'continue' prompt!) — and assert the task completed. The M2b nudge assertion (fifth request is 'continue') moves to... the clean-empty CLI tests already pin the nudge shape. But THIS test's raison d'être is "auto-continued runs get the nudge LIKE ANY RUN" — the M2b regression pin. If I change the scripted empty to be consumed by the in-loop hiccup retry, the test no longer exercises the nudge-after-auto-continue path at all. To keep the M2b pin, the continuation must answer with a CLEAN empty (no tool activity anywhere in the turn's window) — but the funnel scenario inherently has tool activity...

Hmm. What does M2b actually pin? "auto-continued runs get the nudge like any run — the old !isAutoContinue exclusion left a degenerate continuation idle forever (silent after the compaction, again)". The CORE property: an auto-continued run's empty answer is NOT silently accepted; recovery fires. Post-gh-1577, for this scenario the recovery is the hiccup retry (STRONGER than the nudge: 3 attempts). The clean-empty nudge-after-auto-continue case: e.g. over-window continuation that answers empty with NO tool activity in the window — can't construct here.

Actually — wait. Can the funnel scenario produce a clean empty? The window scan stops at the last UserMessage. The nudge 'continue' ADDS a UserMessage! So: toolTurn → 'S' → 'S' → empty(hiccup retried ×3, all empty → exhaustion error)... no nudge at all. To exercise the nudge after an auto-continue, I'd need the FIRST completion of the continued run to be clean-empty — impossible in this funnel shape.

Let me look at what the test SHOULD become per the ticket's test matrix: REG-1: "existing nudge tests (#1085 M2b) run unchanged — `cleanEmpty` → exactly one nudge → settle". The M2b-specific REG-1 tests are the two in agent_cli_test.dart (clean empties, nudged once, settle). THIS over-window test is an INTEGRATION of the funnel + nudge; under gh-1577 its empty continuation becomes a hiccup — the test must be updated to the new expected behavior (the ticket's IT-matrix explicitly anticipates updating: "REG-1: existing nudge tests run unchanged" applies to the CLEAN-empty ones; this one is neither clean nor purely a nudge test anymore).

My update plan for `agent_cli_over_window_continuation_retry_test.dart`:
- Keep the funnel script identical, but the empty continuation now hiccup-recovers: script the 5th call as the in-loop RETRY returning 'continued fine after retry' — wait, no: the hiccup retry re-streams with the SAME context (no new user message). The FakeStreamFunction just replays the next scripted turn — the retry consumes script slot 5 → healthy text → run completes. calls == 5 ✓ same count! Assertions change:
  - output contains the recovered text ✓ (rename to keep meaning)
  - the 5th request is NOT a 'continue' nudge — it's an in-loop retry: `fake.contexts[4].messages.whereType<UserMessage>().last` == 'go' (the original user text, no 'continue' appended) — assert THAT (pins the hiccup-retry shape).
  - name/intent: the continuation's empty is a gh-1577 hiccup, recovered in-loop.

But then the M2b "nudge after auto-continue" property loses its dedicated pin... Add a clean-empty M2b test if not already covered: agent_cli_test.dart's two tests ARE clean empties on FIRST-run (not auto-continued). Hmm — is there another auto-continue nudge test? The M2b change specifically added the over-window funnel test I'm looking at. To preserve its M2b coverage, I could make the funnel's continuation-empty CLEAN by ending the window with... no.

Alternative: keep the funnel+empty script but make the empty's window clean — impossible.

OK here's the cleanest resolution honoring BOTH cards:
1. Update the funnel test to pin the hiccup-recovery (5 calls, no 'continue' prompt, recovered answer, exit... REPL — recovered text visible).
2. The M2b property for auto-continues: add a focused test in agent_cli_test.dart? Hmm — what auto-continue paths exist besides the funnel? `/compact`? The 'continue' nudge on auto-continued runs — the ONLY auto-continue producer is the over-window funnel (isAutoContinue: true recursion) and... `_runPrompt('continue', isAutoContinue: true)` IS the nudge itself. So "nudge after auto-continue" only arises in the funnel scenario. Post-gh-1577, a funnel empty is hiccup-classified and the nudge is RESERVED for clean empties — meaning M2b's nudge-after-auto-continue is now reachable only when the funnel's continuation turn has NO partial content — i.e. the PRE-continuation turns must contain no tool activity... the funnel fires after a post-run compaction of an over-window transcript — the transcript almost always has tools.

Honestly — the M2b nudge semantics that survive gh-1577 are: clean empties get nudged regardless of isAutoContinue. With my change, the empty turn after TOOL ACTIVITY classifies `emptyAfterPartial` → the LOOP (maxEmptyRetries=0) skips generic, then hiccup-retries: empty #2 would consume call 5 (which the test expects to be the NUDGE with prompt 'continue'), then empty #3, #4, exhaustion error — the test's `fake.calls == 5` and nudge assertions would break... AND MORE IMPORTANTLY — is the test's semantic still desired?? 

Per gh-1577: an empty after tool activity is EXACTLY the incident shape — it should hiccup-retry, NOT nudge. This pinned test pins the OLD (buggy) behavior... but wait — does it? The test's intent is #1085 M2b: "auto-continued runs get the nudge like any run". The scenario: over-window relief → auto-continued run → empty answer. The turn HAS tool activity (the tool turn at the start) — so under gh-1577 the empty is a hiccup (bounded retry), and the nudge would only fire for clean empties.

Hmm — this is a genuine semantic CONFLICT between the old pinned test and the new card. The ticket says: "AC2 — A clean empty completion with no partial content anywhere in the turn keeps today's behavior exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle." — this test's empty is NOT clean (tool activity in the turn). So the test needs UPDATING to reflect the new classification: either the scripted history changes so the empty is genuinely clean (hard — the whole point is the over-window funnel), or the test now expects the hiccup behavior (retries then... the 'continue' nudge never fires → the test's M2b assertion needs a clean-empty variant).

Wait — let me think about what the RIGHT behavior is for this scenario post-gh-1577: over-window funnel auto-continues the run; the continuation comes back EMPTY after a turn full of tool activity. gh-1577: hiccup → 3 in-loop retries (backoff) → if still empty → run error (loud). The nudge path is not involved. The M2b property ("auto-continued runs get the nudge like any run") survives for CLEAN empties — which the agent_cli_test.dart REG-1 tests already pin (they're plain textTurn('') with no tools).

So this pinned test needs a rework: the empty after the funnel continuation is now a hiccup. Options:
(a) Change the scripted continuation-empty to a CLEAN empty: impossible — the turn includes the tool turn (same logical turn; the funnel's continuation is an auto-continue within the same logical user turn).

Hmm wait — actually, what IS "the turn" for the classifier here? The window = messages after the last UserMessage. In this scenario: user 'go' → toolTurn → relief/funnel 'S' (assistant texts) → empty. All after the last UserMessage → window has tool activity + text → emptyAfterPartial. Yes — hiccup.

(b) Update the test to pin the NEW behavior: the empty continuation gets hiccup-retried; script [toolTurn, 'S', 'S', empty, healthy('nudged continuation fine' → 'continued fine')] — the loop recovers via retry (call 5 = in-loop retry, context has NO 'continue' prompt!) — and assert the task completed. The M2b nudge assertion (fifth request is 'continue') moves to... the clean-empty CLI tests already pin the nudge shape. But THIS test's raison d'être is "auto-continued runs get the nudge LIKE ANY RUN" — the M2b regression pin. If I change the scripted empty to be consumed by the in-loop hiccup retry, the test no longer exercises the nudge-after-auto-continue path at all. To keep the M2b pin, the continuation must answer with a CLEAN empty (no tool activity anywhere in the turn's window) — but the funnel scenario inherently has tool activity...

Hmm. What does M2b actually pin? "auto-continued runs get the nudge like any run — the old !isAutoContinue exclusion left a degenerate continuation idle forever (silent after the compaction, again)". The CORE property: an auto-continued run's empty answer is NOT silently accepted; recovery fires. Post-gh-1577, for this scenario the recovery is the hiccup retry (STRONGER than the nudge: 3 attempts). The clean-empty nudge-after-auto-continue case: e.g. over-window continuation that answers empty with NO tool activity in the window — can't construct here.

Actually — wait. Can the funnel scenario produce a clean empty? The window scan stops at the last UserMessage. The nudge 'continue' ADDS a UserMessage! So: toolTurn → 'S' → 'S' → empty(hiccup retried ×3, all empty → exhaustion error)... no nudge at all. To exercise the nudge after an auto-continue, I'd need the FIRST completion of the continued run to be clean-empty — impossible in this funnel shape.

Let me look at what the test SHOULD become per the ticket's test matrix: REG-1: "existing nudge tests (#1085 M2b) run unchanged — `cleanEmpty` → exactly one nudge → settle". The M2b-specific REG-1 tests are the two in agent_cli_test.dart (clean empties, nudged once, settle). THIS over-window test is an INTEGRATION of the funnel + nudge; under gh-1577 its empty continuation becomes a hiccup — the test must be updated to the new expected behavior (the ticket's IT-matrix explicitly anticipates updating: "REG-1: existing nudge tests run unchanged" applies to the CLEAN-empty ones; this one is neither clean nor purely a nudge test anymore).

My update plan for `agent_cli_over_window_continuation_retry_test.dart`:
- Keep the funnel script identical, but the empty continuation now hiccup-recovers: script the 5th call as the in-loop RETRY returning 'continued fine after retry' — wait, no: the hiccup retry re-streams with the SAME context (no new user message). The FakeStreamFunction just replays the next scripted turn — the retry consumes script slot 5 → healthy text → run completes. calls == 5 ✓ same count! Assertions change:
  - output contains the recovered text ✓ (rename to keep meaning)
  - the 5th request is NOT a 'continue' nudge — it's an in-loop retry: `fake.contexts[4].messages.whereType<UserMessage>().last` == 'go' (the original user text, no 'continue' appended) — assert THAT (pins the hiccup-retry shape).
  - name/intent: the continuation's empty is a gh-1577 hiccup, recovered in-loop.

But then the M2b "nudge after auto-continue" property loses its dedicated pin... Add a clean-empty M2b test if not already covered: agent_cli_test.dart's two tests ARE clean empties on FIRST-run (not auto-continued). Hmm — is there another auto-continue nudge test? The M2b change specifically added the over-window funnel test I'm looking at. To preserve its M2b coverage, I could make the funnel's continuation-empty CLEAN by ending the window with... no.

Alternative: keep the funnel+empty script but make the empty's window clean — impossible.

OK here's the cleanest resolution honoring BOTH cards:
1. Update the funnel test to pin the hiccup-recovery (5 calls, no 'continue' prompt, recovered answer, exit... REPL — recovered text visible).
2. The M2b property for auto-continues: add a focused test in agent_cli_test.dart? Hmm — what auto-continue paths exist besides the funnel? `/compact`? The 'continue' nudge on auto-continued runs — the ONLY auto-continue producer is the over-window funnel (isAutoContinue: true recursion) and... `_runPrompt('continue', isAutoContinue: true)` IS the nudge itself. So "nudge after auto-continue" only arises in the funnel scenario. Post-gh-1577, a funnel empty is hiccup-classified and the nudge is RESERVED for clean empties — meaning M2b's nudge-after-auto-continue is now reachable only when the funnel's continuation turn has NO partial content — i.e. the PRE-continuation turns must contain no tool activity... the funnel fires after a post-run compaction of an over-window transcript — the transcript almost always has tools.

Honestly — the M2b nudge semantics that survive gh-1577 are: clean empties get nudged regardless of isAutoContinue. I can construct a DIRECT test of that: drive `_settleAfterPrompt` indirectly... simplest true-to-M2b test: the over-window funnel whose continuation answers empty AND whose window is clean — constru…

I found a pinned test (`agent_cli_over_window_continuation_retry_test.dart`) that will conflict: its empty-after-tool-activity continuation is exactly the gh-1577 hiccup shape now. Let me check the background suite results:

One more: **image_registry** / transformContext on retried requests — `_buildRequestContext` runs per attempt ✓.

Now — CRITICAL correctness re-check on the E5 abort conversion: `cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)`. `_isDegenerateEmpty` requires stop==stop. If the cancel produced an aborted message (typical), `_isDegenerateEmpty` is false → no conversion ✓ (message already aborted → `_terminalRunMessages` handles). If the cancel raced (empty stop message), convert ✓.

But hold on — there's a subtle issue: `cancelled` is ALSO true when the run-idle WATCHDOG fired (`run.source.cancel(error)` with RunIdleWatchdogFire) — after which a replay... the watchdog cancel: `_streamAssistantResponse` would surface aborted. Same handling ✓.

Another subtle case: cancel arrives while the loop is streaming a HEALTHY (non-empty) response — `cancelled=true`, `current`=healthy → the while loop: classify(notEmpty) → break → `cancelled && _isDegenerateEmpty(current)` false → return healthy message → run continues normally to TurnEnd... wait, is that the OLD behavior? Old code: while condition checked `_isDegenerateEmpty(current) && retries < max && !cancelled` — with healthy current, loop never ran; the cancel would surface at the next boundary (`_terminalRunMessages` only for error/aborted — a healthy message with a cancelled token continues the run?? The tool phase etc. — pre-existing behavior; the cancel eventually aborts a later stream or the host settles). My change doesn't alter that path (healthy + cancelled → return healthy, same as old) ✓.

if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

blocks.text:
The classifier looks good. One subtle detail I want to re-verify: in `_turnCarriesPartialContent`, the `identical` self-skip — if `message` appears in `turnHistory` but NOT by identity (a copy), the scan would iterate into it (harmless: its content is empty) and then continue PAST it toward older messages — correct anyway.

One more edge: `turnHistory.reversed` — after skipping self, if the previous entry is a UserMessage we break — clean window ✓.

Edge: what if `message` is NOT in turnHistory at all (caller passed a truncated history)? `sawMessage` stays false; we scan everything from the tail until a UserMessage — correct window semantics ✓.

Now — the `1 << attempt.clamp(0, 20)` overflow: baseDelay ms up to large values × 2^20 — int math in Dart is 64-bit, no overflow concern. Matches the roles policy shape (which has the same pattern; the memory note about `1 << (attempt-1)` overflow in HubClient with attempt 65+ — my clamp(0,20) prevents that ✓).

## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"## gh-1577 — Empty completion after truncated stream is a retryable hiccup, never a silent exit 0

### What changed
- An empty assistant completion that follows partial content (assistant text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is now a **bounded-retry provider hiccup** in the agent loop; on retry exhaustion the run ends with a loud `StopReason.error` naming the hiccup, attempt count and last stop reason — headless `-p` exits 1, interactive prints the error and returns to the prompt. The silent exit-0 settle is gone.
- A clean empty (no partial content anywhere in the turn) keeps the #1085 M2b semantics exactly: one `continue` nudge per logical turn, then settle.

### Key decisions
- New pure classifier `classifyEmptyCompletion(turnHistory, message)` (`lib/src/agent/empty_completion.dart`) with verdicts `notEmpty` / `emptyAfterPartial` / `cleanEmpty` / `abortedOrError` — shared by the loop's retry machinery and the CLI's nudge gate; the partial-content window is the TURN (messages after the last user message), so an old truncation can never resurrect retries (E1).
- Truncation signals: `StopReason.length` plus the tolerated silent-truncation `errorMessage` flag count as partial-context evidence (E6); the `ToolCall` boundary survives — thinking-only turns with tool calls are never empty (AC6/E4).
- Retry policy lives in the loop (`agent_loop_empty_completion.dart`, a `part of agent_loop.dart` to stay under the 2800-line gate): `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3, knob alongside `maxEmptyRetries`), exponential backoff in the model-roles `retry.baseDelayMs`/`maxBackoffMs` shape (500ms → 8s cap, deterministic), re-streamed through `_streamAssistantResponse`; retried empties stay in the transcript. `CancelToken` is honored between attempts; an abort racing the classification settles `aborted` (exit 130) — never the hiccup error, never a silent empty (E2/E5).
- Exhaustion reuses `StopReason.error` (open question 2) — the existing headless exit-code switch maps it to 1 with no switch change; the legacy `maxEmptyRetries` budget and the CLI's `maxEmptyRetries: 0` wiring are untouched.
- REG-2 scope note: the never-exit-0 contract is enforced for the hiccup family (empty after partial content) across the `stop` / length-flagged / silent-truncation-flagged paths; the clean-empty settle after its one nudge keeps AC2's pinned exit-0 behavior (REG-1).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/empty_completion_test.dart test/agent/agent_loop_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_empty_completion_hiccup_test.dart
dart test --exclude-tags integration   # full gate suite
```

### Test coverage
- UT-1..UT-5: classifier verdicts incl. thinking+ToolCall not empty, whitespace-only empty, backoff sequence.
- IT-1: `partial → empty → healthy` recovers and finishes (exit 0, retried empty in transcript). IT-2/E3: `partial → empty ×(N+1)` fires exactly N retries then the loud error. IT-3/REG-2: headless exhaustion exits 1 across all stop-reason variants. IT-4/AC5: interactive exhaustion returns to a steerable prompt. REG-1: clean-empty one-nudge tests unchanged.
- UT/IT run in the default CI shard (files verified bin-packed by `shard_files.py`); E2E-1 (live provider lane) and the REG required-check job wiring are CI-config follow-ups, no code dependency.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[assistant completion] --> C{classifyEmptyCompletion}
  C -->|notEmpty / abortedOrError| OWN[existing terminal paths]
  C -->|cleanEmpty| NUDGE[one continue nudge, then settle - #1085 M2b unchanged]
  C -->|emptyAfterPartial| R[bounded retry: N=3, backoff 500ms to 8s]
  R -->|healthy| RUN[turn continues]
  R -->|cancel| AB[settle aborted - exit 130]
  R -->|N retries spent, still empty| ERR[StopReason.error naming hiccup + attempts + last stop]
  ERR -->|headless -p| X1[exit 1]
  ERR -->|interactive| P[error line + prompt stays alive]
```
</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}
